11. Market Power

The economics of the price-setter — monopoly marginal revenue, Cournot reaction functions, and the art of charging each consumer a different price.

  • Monopoly: Marginal Revenue and Deadweight Loss — The monopolist sets price by sliding down the demand curve — which is why marginal revenue MRMRMR falls twice as fast as demand. Profit peaks where MR=MCMR = MCMR=MC, but the red triangle of welfare on the unproduced output evaporates.
  • Cournot Oligopoly — Each firm picks its best output against its rivals' — the reaction functions cross at the Cournot-Nash equilibrium. Push the firm-count NNN slider: at N=1N = 1N=1 it is monopoly, and as NNN grows it converges to competition.
  • Price Discrimination — The art of charging different prices in different markets. Third-degree sets MRi=MCMR_i = MCMRi​=MC per market; first-degree converts all consumer surplus into profit. But third-degree deadweight loss can exceed the uniform-price one — check the calculation that breaks the folk wisdom.
